summary: @ornikar/browserslist-config preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes bundled obfuscated payload
details: The package advertises itself as a browserslist configuration and its config files (degraded-support.js, full-support.js, index.js) each contain only a short comma-separated list of browser targets. However, the tarball also ships an obfuscated preinstall script (setup.mjs) and a 727KB obfuscated bundle (math_init.js) that have no relationship to browserslist. package.json declares scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs". setup.mjs is obfuscated with obfuscator.io-style transforms (hex `_0x...` identifiers, wrapper-object indirection of execFileSync) and constructs the URL https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<asset>, downloads the Bun runtime binary to a temp directory, chmods it 0755, and invokes execFileSync(bunPath, [math_init.js path]) — running the bundled 727KB payload under a freshly fetched second-language runtime rather than under Node, without any signature or hash verification. math_init.js begins with a `// @bun` marker followed by a large string-array + rotator (WV8StW performing array.shift cycling) — the shape of a string-array obfuscator packing an executable payload. This is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern: installing the package pulls Bun and executes an opaque obfuscated bundle at install time on the installer's machine. The composition (small legitimate browserslist config plus large obfuscated dropper) is consistent with a compromised maintainer publish appending an attacker payload to an otherwise legitimate package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
